description: Documentary and historical claims: whether the sources that agree about something are actually saying it independently. The field has no kernel and no dataset to re-analyse — the evidence is documents, and the one operation that cannot be argued with is collapsing the citation graph to its roots.

artifact_kinds: dossier: the sources, their derivation chains, the archives searched, and the transformations the wording passed through
a collapsed citation graph with its surviving independent origins
examples: Three chronicles report the same battle. Are they three independent accounts or one account copied twice?
Does the surviving charter evidence support the claim that this monastery held the mill before the reign in question?
Assess whether the eyewitness testimony in this manuscript tradition is contemporary or a later interpolation.
The historical record contains no mention of the settlement before that century. Does that establish it did not exist?
Trace the provenance of this attested quotation back through the manuscript tradition to a primary source.
Is the prosopographical identification in this critical apparatus supported by anything outside the editor's conjecture?
The grain shipment recorded at Ostia in 212 is attested by two independent origins. Is it?
Two scribes copying the same exemplar share an error at the same place. What does that show?
counter_examples: Trace this bug back through the git history and commit log to the change that introduced it.
Prove that every prime greater than three is congruent to one or five modulo six.
Does knocking down this gene reduce the inflammatory signature in donor macrophages?
Audit the database record and server logs for the period when the outage occurred.

tiers.name: structural
tiers.description: Dossier shape: the claim's dimensions frozen, every source identified, dated, and locatable by shelfmark, every derivation chain terminating inside the declared set, and no citation cycles. Two sources citing each other establish that they cite each other.
tiers.contamination_controls: Reads the dossier and the claim only. It has no access to whether the claim is true and cannot be tuned toward it.

tiers.name: triangulation
tiers.description: Follows every supporting source back along its derivation chain and collapses the agreeing sources to distinct origins. Where the dossier records a COLLATION the kinship is derived rather than read off the declared `origin` field: agreement in error indicates common descent, agreement in a correct reading indicates nothing, and a dossier declaring two origins for witnesses that share two errors fails. With no collation the declared origins stand unchecked, which the receipt records as a gap and never as a finding of independence.
tiers.two_sided_evidence: scripts/negative_control/ holds eight known-bad dossiers the tier must refuse, including one declaring two origins whose readings share two errors; the accepted dossier carries a collation whose witnesses agree in a CORRECT reading and err separately, which is the discriminating case a similarity measure gets backwards. scripts/check.py --self-test runs both directions.
tiers.contamination_controls: The collapse is computed from the declared derivation edges, and the frozen target hash is checked before and after. A dossier cannot be edited to add independence after the count comes back short without changing the hash.

receipt_format.freshness_rule: The receipt records the dossier's SHA-256 at check time and is stale the moment the dossier's current hash differs; the exit gate recomputes rather than trusting the recorded value. Adding a source, or an edge between existing sources, changes the collapse — so a receipt from before an edit is a receipt about a different graph.

escalation.failure_signature: The pair (failure_class, first problem line with source ids, shelfmarks, dates, and counts stripped). Two failures with the same pair are the same failure. Three rather than two, because unlike a recomputation over fixed data, each attempt here can legitimately bring new sources — a second attempt with a genuinely new source is a different attempt even when it fails the same way.

rules.why: whether two sources are really two
how a claim travelled to here

refute_attempt.name: cascade-collapse
refute_attempt.description: The same computation as the triangulation tier, read the other way: the claim asserts N independent supports, the collapse says how many survive. A claim whose corroboration collapses to a single origin has been refuted AS CORROBORATION whether or not it is true, which is the distinction this field exists to keep. Discharged by the triangulation tier because that tier cannot be talked into a false pass.

additional.name: dating-consistency
additional.description: A chain cannot run backwards, and a witness dated a century after the event is not contemporary however early it is relative to the other sources. Dates in a bibliography are read as labels; here they are constraints.

additional.name: survivorship
additional.description: An absence claim must state why a record would have survived, and where the dossier gives a survival-rate interval and a count of recording opportunities the silence is PRICED: P(no surviving record | it happened) = (1-r)^n, judged at the pessimistic end of the interval. A claim whose own arithmetic says the archive would plausibly be silent anyway is a claim about the archive. With no rate stated the tool refuses to invent one and the prose argument stands alone, which the receipt says.

additional.name: transmission-chain
additional.description: Counts the language changes and lossy transformations between the claim and its roots. Past a threshold the key wording must be quoted in the original, because a claim resting on a thrice-translated phrase is a claim about the third translator. A reconstruction or emendation in the chain must say what it changed.

additional.name: interest-audit
additional.description: Not whether a source is biased — interested parties are often the only people present, and discarding them empties the archive. Whether, after collapsing to distinct origins, anything is left that did not want the claim to be true. If every origin shares one stake, their agreement is explained by the stake and needs no other cause.

additional.name: scope-language
additional.description: Documented, attested, and occurred are three different statements written the same way. The distance between the first and the third is the discipline, and prose crosses it for free.

CHECKED_BOUNDED_ATTESTED.description: Two or more origins that survive the collapse, chains in order, transformations accounted for, and at least one origin without a stake in the claim. Bounded by what survived and what was searched, and silent about what did not.

CHECKED_BOUNDED_DOCUMENTED.description: A single surviving origin records this. Legitimate and narrow: it establishes that the thing was written down, in that place, by that hand. It is not attestation and must never be reported with plural wording.

REJECTED_CASCADE.description: Refuted as corroboration: the agreeing sources collapse to fewer origins than the claim asserts. Recorded separately because the claim may still be true — what has been refuted is the reason given for believing it.

reference_data.purpose: The known-bad dossiers this adapter must refuse and the one it must accept, so `adversarial: true` is a test rather than a self-report.
